archetype.name: Lost Season
archetype.definition: A full-season collapse from four straight years near .500 to 65-97: outscored in six of seven months, buried 35 games behind the division winner, and never close to the race.

report.headline: The .500 plateau cracked: a 65-win year without a single winning month

recap.finish: 65-97, fourth in the NL West, 35 games behind LAD; missed the postseason
recap.body:
For four straight seasons the Giants lived at 79 to 81 wins: never good, never bad, run differential hovering near zero. In 2026 the floor gave way. They went 65-97, were outscored 669 to 760 (-0.56 runs per game, 25th of 30), ranked 26th in runs scored and 23rd in runs allowed, and finished 28th on the site. This was not a team undone by one broken unit. It was below average almost everywhere, and the record came in worse than even that implied.

The season never had an upswing. They opened 2-3, went 11-15 in April, and May was the worst of it: 10-18 with 150 runs allowed, nearly 5.4 per game. June (12-14) and July (12-13) were steadier, and July was the only month they outscored opponents, 118-112. Then the bottom fell out again: 10-18 in August and 8-16 in September, an 18-34 finish. Their longest winning streak all year was three games. They closed 2-8, losing the last five, and dropped all six games against the Dodgers in that stretch.

The lineup had a real core and too much dead weight around it. Rafael Devers was the engine, with 37 home runs, a 136 wRC+ and 3.4 WAR. Bryce Eldridge (131 wRC+, .364 OBP) ranked 7th of 36 at DH, and Casey Schmitt hit for power with 21 homers in 409 PA. Beyond those three the production thinned out. Willy Adames got on base at .289, Matt Chapman managed a .368 SLG, and Marcelo Mayer and Christian Koss combined for 466 PA at a 58-59 wRC+. That depth problem is how a group with two 130-plus bats still grades F. The 94 park factor dents raw OPS (.706, 23rd), but wRC+ adjusts for the park, and the holes are still there.

Run prevention failed in layers. The rotation (D+) was better than its ERA. Logan Webb, an All-Star, posted a 4.31 ERA over a 3.45 FIP, and Landen Roupp's 4.01 ERA sat close to a 3.73 FIP despite an 11.4% walk rate. Behind them the defense cost -25.9 Fielding Runs (28th), with Adames alone at -13.4 at shortstop. The bullpen was the bigger problem. It graded F, no reliever topped 0.5 WAR, and the team's saves leader, Joel Kuhnel, had 8 of them with a 5.34 FIP and a 13.9% strikeout rate. Camilo Doval walked 12.1% of hitters. A pen with no one to protect a lead helps explain a -6.6 W vs Run Diff (28th): by margin this was a roughly 72-win team that played to 65.

By the end the roster looked even thinner. Devers, Schmitt, Chapman, Houser, McDonald and Tidwell all finish the year listed on the 60-day injured list. The sheet doesn't say when each went down, but a late-season slide that coincides with that many regulars and starters on the shelf is no surprise.

highlights.title: Devers and Eldridge anchored the lineup
highlights.body: Devers' 37 homers and 136 wRC+ and Eldridge's 131 wRC+ with a .364 OBP gave the Giants two bats that would play in any lineup. Both carried full-season samples, so this is real production, not a hot month. They are the clearest pieces to build the offense around.

highlights.title: Webb pitched better than his ERA
highlights.body: Webb's 3.45 FIP against a 4.31 ERA says he did his part on strikeouts, walks and homers, and a defense that cost 25.9 runs inflated the rest. Roupp's 3.73 FIP backs up a solid second starter. The front of the rotation is more sound than the D+ grade suggests.

lowlights.title: A bullpen with no answers
lowlights.body: The pen graded F, and none of its top five relievers produced more than 0.5 WAR. The closer's job fell to Kuhnel, whose 5.34 FIP and 13.9% strikeout rate don't fit high-leverage work, while Doval and Dylan Smith both walked over 12% of batters. The -6.6 W vs Run Diff follows from that, and it is the part of the record most likely to need new arms rather than luck to fix.

lowlights.title: Lineup holes and leaky defense
lowlights.body: Mayer and Koss gave nearly 470 PA of a 58-59 wRC+, and Adames paired a .289 OBP with -13.4 Def Runs at shortstop. Team Fielding Runs of -25.9 ranked 28th, a third straight season in the red. The infield needs work at the plate and in the field.

lowlights.title: A collapsing final two months
lowlights.body: After a near-.500 June and July, they went 10-18 in August and 8-16 in September, finishing on a five-game losing streak. They never won more than three in a row all year.

arc.note: A bad May, a brief stabilization in June and July (the only month they outscored anyone), then an 18-34 slide through August and September that ended 2-8.

recap.nextYear: The carrying pieces are clear: Devers and Eldridge in the lineup, Webb and Roupp in the rotation, with Schmitt's power a useful third bat. The W vs Run Diff says about seven wins were lost to close-game results, so a neutral year with this talent projects to the low 70s. That is still well short of the 80-win plateau of 2022-25, so luck alone won't restore it. The work is structural. The bullpen needs late-inning arms, the infield needs both on-base ability and better gloves (shortstop and third base most of all), and the rotation needs depth behind its top two, since Houser, McDonald and Tidwell all ended the year on the 60-day list. How quickly the injured regulars return matters too, and the sheet can't say.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; the run differential and every unit's grades point the same way.
